chapter_title: Concerning the Three Days and the Two Deaths
chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly substrate teaching. It presents a systematic cosmological classification of three great days (cosmic narrative of First Man, reign in new aeon, Father's eternal unveiling) and two deaths (mixing of light with darkness, eternal separation of sinful souls). Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system throughout — no contemporary institutions, no application to the editor's world, no editorial bridge. The only editorial material is dialogue framing in ¶1-3 and ¶13. The seam flags on ¶5 and ¶12 are false positives (empty institutional vocabulary). No editorial fatigue pattern. A remarkably clean teaching chapter with a Persian-style enumeration structure.

paragraphs.core_text: There exist three great mighty days in all; and also two great and bitter deaths.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples: Happen you know, my beloved ones, that' — dialogue frame formula ('Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples') and devotional address ('my beloved ones').
paragraphs.temporal_note: Standard dialogue frame formula wrapping a substantive cosmological proposition. The three-days/two-deaths structure is the teaching's skeleton — it defines the enumeration that follows.

paragraphs.core_text: What are these three great days? Or again, what are these two deaths that are bitter?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'When his disciples heard, they say to him: Tell us our father,' — dialogue frame narration and honorific address. The substantive cosmological question is preserved.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The question defines the teaching structure — it IS the substrate. The Persian pedagogical tradition structures teaching through such questions. The frame wrapping ('Tell us our father') is editorial.
Pure dialogue attribution with no cosmological content.

paragraphs.core_text: The first day is our father, the Man. From the time when the First Man went down to the abyss of darkness and drowned in it; and the Living Spirit was sent, who went and bore him up. After the Man had ascended, the Father of Life and the Great Spirit set things in order, and the worlds above and below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First enumeration unit. Maps the first day to the cosmic descent-rescue narrative. All entities (First Man, Living Spirit, Father of Life, Great Spirit) are cosmic agents. 'Our father, the Man' — standard epithet for the First Man within the cosmic system, not editorial devotional address.

paragraphs.core_text: Furthermore, the glorious Ambassador came and dwelt in the ship of the day. He displayed his glorious image, and he purified the light out of all things. He walked in the heights of the heavens. Till the time when the world will be dissolved, all things destroyed, the great fire released, and the Last Statue ascends. These three deeds were begun on this first day, when they sent the First Man with his five sons.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Seam flag is a false positive — the institutional vocabulary field is empty. 'Furthermore' connects cosmic content to cosmic content (Ambassador, ship of the day, purification, great fire, Last Statue, First Man with five sons). All entities and processes are within the cosmic system. This continues and summarizes the first-day teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.103⟩ In contrast, [the first death] is the darkness that mixed with the five sons of the First Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highest substrate density in the chapter (36.84). Maps the first death to a cosmic event — Darkness mixing with the five sons. Both sides pure cosmic domain. 'In contrast' marks the structural alternation between days and deaths.

paragraphs.core_text: The second day is the time when the fathers of light, who were victorious in the struggle, will sit on their thrones in the new aeon and dwell on the new earth. And they reign in the new aeon till the Father unveils his image above them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second enumeration unit. Maps the second day to cosmic eschatology — fathers of light, thrones, new aeon, new earth, Father's unveiling. All within the cosmic system. The 'new aeon' and 'new earth' are cosmic domains, not contemporary institutions.

paragraphs.core_text: The {length of the sojourn} in the new aeon equals the measure of the first day spent in affliction. They will reign like this and rejoice in the new aeon.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological-temporal correspondence: duration of second day equals duration of first day. Maps time-domain to time-domain — a structural correspondence. The {length of the sojourn} preserves the manuscript's gap marker.

paragraphs.core_text: The great third day [is the time] when the Father will unveil over them his image ... ... and he raises them up [ ... ] and he receives them into his hidden treasury ... and he gives [ ... ] his soul. He can pour out upon them ... his ambrosia and his sweet perfume, which takes away all affliction that they have seen with their eyes. [ ... ] fullness and a joy eternal! When his grace would sate them, he gives to them his [ ... ] and they are made anew in them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third enumeration unit — heavily lacunose. The surviving text maps the third day to cosmic restoration: Father's unveiling, hidden treasury, ambrosia, sweet perfume. These are correspondential registers — sensory qualities (perfume, taste) mapped to cosmic processes (restoration, renewal). Despite heavy damage, the substrate structure is clear.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, he can summon them once more in peace and silence, and perfect their stature in same measure as his first aeons. And he sets each power in its aeon, in its dwelling-place. They will dwell in the new aeon in their aeons!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues third-day teaching. 'Perfect their stature in same measure as his first aeons' — cosmic restoration to original measure. 'Sets each power in its aeon, in its dwelling-place' — systematic cosmic ordering, place-assignment. Pure process description.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, when they dwell in their aeons, they will become rich beyond measure, for ever, beyond time. From then on they will not count that season amongst them; nor the number of the days, nor the hours, generation after generation, for ever and ever. The Father will not be hidden from them, from this time on. Rather, he has accomplished (his) unveiling to them [ ... ] he being revealed to them for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Describes the eternal state of the third day — what it IS, not what the audience should do. 'The Father will not be hidden from them' is a cosmic-relational statement. No audience address, no exhortation. The slight exhortation vocabulary score (4.05) comes from devotional-sounding phrases ('for ever and ever') but these describe cosmic eternity, not moral application. The 'Now' opener is a transitional particle, not an editorial bridge.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the three great days, [which the Father of Greatness has given number to in the reckoning].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Recapitulation formula closing the three-days enumeration. Seam flag is false positive — empty institutional vocabulary. 'These are the three great days' is a standard enumeration closure integral to the teaching structure. The restored text attributes the three-fold numbering to the Father of Greatness — cosmic attribution, not editorial.

paragraphs.core_text: In contrast, the two deaths are these.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'that I have proclaimed to you' — first-person dialogue attribution addressing the audience, not cosmological content.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Structural transition from the three-days to the two-deaths enumeration. 'In contrast' parallels the same phrase in ¶6, marking the alternation. The first-person 'I have proclaimed to you' is dialogue frame inserted into the transition.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.104⟩ The first death is from the time when the light fell to the darkness, and was mixed in with the rulers of Darkness; until the time when the light will become pure, and be separated from the darkness in that great fire. The remainder left behind there can build and add to that Last Statue.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Expands on the first death introduced in ¶6. Maps it to the full cosmic process: light falling, mixing with rulers of Darkness, purification in great fire, Last Statue. Both sides entirely within the cosmic system. 'Rulers of Darkness' capitalized as personified cosmic agents.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, the second death is the death in which the souls of sinful men shall die; when [they will] be stripped of the shining light that illuminates the world. And also they are separated from the living air, from which they receive [living] breath; and they are deprived of this living soul, which [ ... ] in the world; and they are separated and swept away from this Last Statue [ ... ... ] and bound on [ ... ... ] the female will become [ ... ] their torture and their affliction; for their deeds [ ... ] those three places; because they have blasphemed and despised the Holy Spirit since [ev]ery generation of the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Maps the second death to systematic cosmic separation: stripped of shining light, separated from living air, deprived of living soul, swept from Last Statue. This is a correspondential stripping sequence — the cosmic elements (light, air, soul) are removed one by one. 'Sinful men' is a cosmic category, not contemporary moral address. 'Blasphemed the Holy Spirit' describes rejection of a cosmic entity. 'Since every generation of the world' is cosmic temporal framing. The moral language stays within the system — it describes WHAT happens and WHY, not an exhortation to avoid it. Heavy lacunae in the second half.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the two deaths. The first death is temporal; [but] the second death is eternal. It is the sec[ond deat]h!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Recapitulation formula closing the two-deaths enumeration, paralleling ¶12's closure of the three-days. The temporal/eternal distinction is a cosmological classification. 'It is the second death!' — emphatic closing. The phrase 'second death' occurs in Revelation 20:14, but here it arises naturally from the teaching's own two-deaths structure without citation markers. The substrate builds this term from scratch through enumeration.
